-- Additive schema draft. Integrator assigns the next migration number; never
-- replace an applied migration. All epoch timestamps are milliseconds.
CREATE TABLE oa_operators (
 id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, display_name TEXT NOT NULL,
 role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(role IN ('owner','admin','member')),
 status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(status IN ('invited','active','inactive')),
 version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE oa_bootstrap (singleton INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK(singleton=1), claim_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, claimed_at INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE oa_tokens (
 id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, token_hash TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
 kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(kind IN ('magic','invite')),
 operator_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES oa_operators(id), operator_version INTEGER NOT NULL,
 issuer_id TEXT REFERENCES oa_operators(id), issuer_version INTEGER,
 return_to TEXT NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
 consumed_at INTEGER, revoked_at INTEGER,
 CHECK((kind='invite' AND issuer_id IS NOT NULL AND issuer_version IS NOT NULL)
    OR (kind='magic' AND issuer_id IS NULL AND issuer_version IS NULL))
);
CREATE TABLE oa_sessions (
 id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, token_hash TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
 operator_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES oa_operators(id), operator_version INTEGER NOT NULL,
 kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(kind IN ('native','review','oidc','password')),
 source_token_id TEXT UNIQUE REFERENCES oa_tokens(id),
 created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL, revoked_at INTEGER
);
CREATE INDEX oa_sessions_operator ON oa_sessions(operator_id);
CREATE TABLE oa_external_identities (
 issuer TEXT NOT NULL, subject TEXT NOT NULL, operator_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES oa_operators(id),
 PRIMARY KEY(issuer, subject)
);
CREATE TABLE oa_limits (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, window INTEGER NOT NULL, count INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TRIGGER oa_preserve_last_owner_update BEFORE UPDATE OF status,role ON oa_operators
 WHEN OLD.role='owner' AND OLD.status='active' AND (NEW.role!='owner' OR NEW.status!='active')
 AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM oa_operators WHERE role='owner' AND status='active') <= 1
 BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'last_owner'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER oa_preserve_last_owner_delete BEFORE DELETE ON oa_operators
 WHEN OLD.role='owner' AND OLD.status='active'
 AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM oa_operators WHERE role='owner' AND status='active') <= 1
 BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'last_owner'); END;
-- A status/role change invalidates every preexisting session and link, including
-- after a later reactivation. Keep this invariant for direct administrative SQL.
CREATE TRIGGER oa_operator_version AFTER UPDATE OF status,role ON oa_operators
 WHEN OLD.status != NEW.status OR OLD.role != NEW.role
 BEGIN UPDATE oa_operators SET version=OLD.version+1 WHERE id=NEW.id; END;

-- Fresh installs include the additive invitation cancellation ledger.
-- Apply as a NEW numbered migration after operator-auth.sql in existing stores.
-- This durable record is admission state, not an expiring credential. Never prune it.
-- Existing active/inactive operators retain their recorded status: no historical
-- acceptance is inferred. Only a witnessed invited -> inactive transition records
-- an unaccepted cancellation, including direct administrative SQL transitions.
CREATE TABLE oa_invitation_cancellations (
 operator_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES oa_operators(id),
 operator_version INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE TRIGGER oa_record_invitation_cancellation AFTER UPDATE OF status ON oa_operators
 WHEN OLD.status='invited' AND NEW.status='inactive'
 BEGIN INSERT INTO oa_invitation_cancellations(operator_id,operator_version)
 VALUES(NEW.id,OLD.version+1)
 ON CONFLICT(operator_id) DO UPDATE SET operator_version=excluded.operator_version; END;
CREATE TRIGGER oa_reject_cancelled_invitation_reactivation BEFORE UPDATE OF status ON oa_operators
 WHEN NEW.status='active' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM oa_invitation_cancellations WHERE operator_id=OLD.id)
 BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'invitation_required'); END;

migrations.sql:
-- Agent and deploy keys are fenced with the person whose session minted them:
-- each records that person and their identity fence (oa_operators.version) at
-- minting, and counts only while that person is active at that same version. A
-- fence from the linked Auth install or a suspension moves the version, so the
-- keys never count again. Spool's API mints only from the owner's session, so
-- keys minted before this record the current owner.
ALTER TABLE credentials ADD COLUMN minted_by TEXT;
ALTER TABLE credentials ADD COLUMN minted_version INTEGER;
UPDATE credentials SET minted_by=(SELECT id FROM oa_operators WHERE role='owner' AND status='active' ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 1),
 minted_version=(SELECT version FROM oa_operators WHERE role='owner' AND status='active' ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 1)
 WHERE kind IN ('agent','deploy');

migrations.name: 0030_owner_erasure_credential_authority.sql
migrations.sql:
-- Durable credential authority after any owner erasure (0028 freezes writes only
-- while the operation runs). An earlier release created these triggers at request
-- time when the first erasure began; replace them here.
-- A new credential must name the active owner at the identity fence it was
-- minted under, so a predecessor mint admitted before the handoff and resumed
-- after it is refused. An existing credential may afterwards only be revoked:
-- revocation never depends on who minted the key or on a later identity fence.
-- The erasure's own guarded batch clears the erased owner's ingest-key attribution.
DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS spool_erased_owner_credential_insert;
DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS spool_erased_owner_credential_update;
CREATE TRIGGER spool_erased_owner_credential_insert BEFORE INSERT ON credentials
WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM rer_erasure_operations WHERE entity='installation-owner')
 AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM oa_operators o WHERE o.id=NEW.minted_by AND o.version=NEW.minted_version AND o.status='active' AND o.role='owner')
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'credential_authority_changed'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER spool_erased_owner_credential_update BEFORE UPDATE ON credentials
WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM rer_erasure_operations WHERE entity='installation-owner') AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM rer_erasure_guard)
 AND (NEW.revoked IS NULL OR NEW.hash IS NOT OLD.hash OR NEW.project IS NOT OLD.project OR NEW.kind IS NOT OLD.kind OR NEW.created IS NOT OLD.created
  OR NEW.minted_by IS NOT OLD.minted_by OR NEW.minted_version IS NOT OLD.minted_version)
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'credential_authority_changed'); END;

-- Every committed change records one attributed safe fact in its own transaction.
-- A writer opens one context row inside its batch (actor, action, subject and
-- project aliases, all already safe) and closes it before the batch ends. A
-- change commits its fact by marking the context committed: either by writing
-- the operational journal (`audit`), which requires a context, or explicitly.
-- An aborted batch rolls back the change, the context and the fact together.
CREATE TABLE audit_context (
 slot INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK(slot=1),
 actor_kind TEXT NOT NULL,
 actor_label TEXT NOT NULL,
 action TEXT NOT NULL,
 subject_kind TEXT NOT NULL,
 subject_label TEXT NOT NULL,
 project_label TEXT,
 created INTEGER NOT NULL,
 committed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK(committed IN (0,1))
);
CREATE TRIGGER audit_context_commit AFTER UPDATE OF committed ON audit_context WHEN OLD.committed=0 AND NEW.committed=1 BEGIN
 INSERT INTO spool_audit_events(id,created,source,actor_kind,actor_label,action,subject_kind,subject_label,project_label,outcome,status)
 VALUES(lower(hex(randomblob(4)))||'-'||lower(hex(randomblob(2)))||'-'||lower(hex(randomblob(2)))||'-'||lower(hex(randomblob(2)))||'-'||lower(hex(randomblob(6))),
  NEW.created,'transaction',NEW.actor_kind,NEW.actor_label,NEW.action,NEW.subject_kind,NEW.subject_label,NEW.project_label,'succeeded',NULL);
END;
-- Restore drops and recreates this trigger around its own copy, so restored
-- journal rows never become new facts attributed to the restoring actor.
CREATE TRIGGER audit_journal_fact AFTER INSERT ON audit BEGIN
 SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'audit_context_required') WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM audit_context);
 UPDATE audit_context SET committed=1;
END;

-- Journal kinds written before attributed facts existed. Their permanent copy
-- keeps kind-derived action, time and outcome only: actor unknown, fresh

-- marker row (ord 0) records that the archive carried safe history at all.
CREATE TABLE audit_restore_staging (import_id TEXT NOT NULL, ord INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(ord>=0), fact TEXT, PRIMARY KEY(import_id,ord));

CREATE TRIGGER audit_restore_commit AFTER UPDATE OF import_job ON rer_portability_state WHEN OLD.import_job IS NOT NULL AND NEW.import_job IS NULL BEGIN

  SELECT json_extract(fact,'$.id'),json_extract(fact,'$.created'),json_extract(fact,'$.source'),json_extract(fact,'$.actor_kind'),json_extract(fact,'$.actor_label'),

  FROM audit_restore_staging WHERE OLD.applying=1 AND import_id=OLD.import_job AND ord>0 ORDER BY ord;
 -- Previous archive formats carry no safe history: their restored journal rows get legacy facts.
 INSERT INTO audit_legacy_labels SELECT project,'audit:'||lower(hex(randomblob(16))) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT project FROM audit WHERE project IS NOT NULL)
  WHERE OLD.applying=1 AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM audit_restore_staging WHERE import_id=OLD.import_job);

  SELECT lower(hex(randomblob(4)))||'-'||lower(hex(randomblob(2)))||'-'||lower(hex(randomblob(2)))||'-'||lower(hex(randomblob(2)))||'-'||lower(hex(randomblob(6))),
   a.created,'legacy','unknown','audit:'||lower(hex(randomblob(16))),COALESCE(m.action,'private.action'),COALESCE(m.subject_kind,'unknown'),'audit:'||lower(hex(randomblob(16))),

  FROM audit a LEFT JOIN audit_legacy_actions m ON m.kind=a.kind
  WHERE OLD.applying=1 AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM audit_restore_staging WHERE import_id=OLD.import_job) ORDER BY a.created,a.id;
